statement: Create schedules of elements, components or surfaces listing parameters and properties in columns, saved as navigator views that edit and refresh against the model.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule

superiority: Single schedule engine over any element type with sub-second incremental update.

acceptance.sketch: Schedule of 40 walls lists 40 rows; editing a wall width in the model changes the cell without refresh.

notes: VERIFIED — read Interactive Schedule; three list types (element, component, surface), predefined schemes in template.

statement: List the components of composite, profile and basic elements as rows, with component type, thickness, volumes, areas and the building material's data, optionally keeping each element's components together.

source.ref: Component Data in Archicad

superiority: Components for every parametric element, not only walls.

acceptance.sketch: Composite wall with 3 skins gives 3 rows whose volumes sum to the wall volume.

notes: CORRECTED — components are skins of composites, fills of profiles and single components of basic elements; stair and railing parts have separate listing parameters. Read Component Data in Archicad, Component Listing Parameters.

statement: List the visible surfaces of elements with exposed areas per surface for finish take-off, with predefined schemes such as all finishes and finishes by element.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Surface Schedules

superiority: Face-level surface take-off with orientation.

acceptance.sketch: Sum of surface areas per material equals analytic total.

notes: VERIFIED — read Surface Schedules and Surface Schedule: Predefined schemes.

statement: Define a schedule scheme with an ID, name and type, criteria and fields, sort order and display settings, and import or export schemes among projects as XML.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Schedule contents: Criteria and fields

superiority: Schemes are JSON documents that can be stored in version control.

acceptance.sketch: Save and reopen scheme: criteria, fields and sort order identical.

notes: CORRECTED — scheme dialog holds criteria and fields; sorting is a per-field setting; schemes import/export as XML. Read Create a new schedule, Schedule contents: Criteria and fields.

statement: Filter listed items with criteria joined by AND and OR, with open and close parentheses for nesting, an invalid-criteria warning for unbalanced groups, and the same criteria model as find and select.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Add Criteria

superiority: Criteria shared with queries, graphic overrides and Python.

acceptance.sketch: Criteria Layer = A OR Layer = B AND Height > 2 returns expected count.

notes: CORRECTED — multiple element types are joined with OR, parentheses columns nest, shared with Find & Select. Read Add Criteria: Which elements should be listed?, Define Element Criteria.

statement: Express each criterion as a parameter or property with a chosen value, including classification tests (is, is not, under) and defined or undefined tests for properties.

source.ref: Property Availability for Classifications (criteria tests)

superiority: Regex and range operators in addition.

acceptance.sketch: Each documented test returns exactly the matching elements on a mixed data set, including elements with an undefined property.

notes: CORRECTED — full operator list (begins with, greater than, one of) not shown in cached help; only classification and defined/undefined tests confirmed. Read Property Availability, Define Element Criteria.

statement: Choose schedule fields from parameters, properties, classifications and library part parameters in a searchable list, ordered with up/down controls and sized per row or column.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Add Fields

superiority: Computed columns at cell-level.

acceptance.sketch: Reorder columns persists to the printed schedule.

notes: VERIFIED — read Add Fields: Which data do you want to list?; blue fields are editable, black are not.

statement: Edit the main header and field header texts, show or hide them, and insert merged group headers above adjacent column headers.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Main Headers and Field Headers

superiority: Localised headers per language.

acceptance.sketch: A renamed header persists after save and reopen.

notes: CORRECTED — headers editable by typing or field settings, merged headers and freeze documented; alignment and units belong to other settings. Read Main Headers and Field Headers.

statement: Order fields and sort by any field ascending or descending, and flag one field to subdivide the listing into totals.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Sorting order

superiority: Multi-level grouping with live subtotals.

acceptance.sketch: Group by type shows count and sums.

notes: CORRECTED — sort arrows per field; grouping with count and subtotals is done by flagging one field for totals. Read Sorting order, Display Grand Totals and Totals.

statement: Add grand-total sums for numeric fields, grand-total item counts, and per-subdivision totals for a flagged field, with optional unit display and custom prefix and suffix text.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Display Grand Totals and Totals

superiority: Aggregates have formulas visible.

acceptance.sketch: Total equals sum of rows to 1e-9.

notes: VERIFIED — read Display Grand Totals and Totals; grand totals can use displayed rounded values or exact values per Calculation Rules.

statement: Merge identical records into one row, with a per-field choice to include the field in merged records even when its values differ.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Merge identical records

superiority: Merge key is configurable.

acceptance.sketch: Merging 10 identical doors gives one row with quantity 10.

notes: CORRECTED — merge is a switch on identical records with a per-field 'any value' option; quantity comes from a count field. Read Merge identical records.

statement: Select scheduled items in the floor plan or 3D window from selected rows, with elements on hidden or locked layers neither selectable nor editable.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Select Schedule Items on Floor Plan/3D

superiority: Bidirectional selection across all views.

acceptance.sketch: Row click selects exactly element GUID.

notes: CORRECTED — row to model selection documented with the locked/hidden layer limit; the reverse (list floor-plan selection) is a separate command. Read Select Schedule Items on Floor Plan/3D, Scheduled Elements on Locked or Hidden Layer.

statement: Edit blue editable fields directly in the schedule so changes apply immediately to the model, and model edits refresh the schedule when it is reopened.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Edit the model using Interactive Schedule

superiority: Undo is shared with the model.

acceptance.sketch: Editing an ID cell updates the element ID in the model and undo reverses it.

notes: VERIFIED — read Edit the model using Interactive Schedule and Editing and Updating Schedule Items.

statement: Show overridden values and restore defaults.

source.ref: Schedule: override flags (not found)

superiority: Overrides are highlighted.

acceptance.sketch: Reset restores the default value and clears the override flag.

notes: REJECTED: no override-flag or restore-default feature in schedules in Archicad 30 help; only Reset Custom Colors exists. Default linking is a property feature (chain icon), covered by PROPS rows.

statement: Provide element listing parameters for each construction and library element type, including walls, slabs, roofs, columns, beams, doors, windows, zones, objects, curtain wall parts, stairs, railings and MEP elements.

source.ref: Element Listing Parameters

superiority: Uniform behaviour across all element types.

acceptance.sketch: A schedule of each element type returns the expected count.

notes: CORRECTED — help organises parameters per element type with a general set. Read Element Listing Parameters, General Listing Parameters.

statement: Save a schedule as a view and place it on a layout as a drawing that stays linked to the model data.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule

superiority: Paginated tables with repeat headers.

acceptance.sketch: Schedule drawing on layout shows updated data after change.

notes: CORRECTED — layout placement documented; page-break handling is done by restructure and split commands (see separate rows). Read Interactive Schedule, Schedules placed on Layouts.

statement: Save a schedule from its window as tabbed text, DWF, XLS, PDF or on Windows DOC, or copy it into a 2D window as a non-interactive object.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Save from Schedule Window

superiority: Round trip through spreadsheet updates model.

acceptance.sketch: Tabbed-text export values equal on-screen values, with units shown as displayed.

notes: CORRECTED — formats are tabbed text, DWF, XLS, DOC (Windows) and PDF; CSV, XLSX, XML and HTML not listed. Read Save Project, Interactive Schedule.

statement: Show editable dimensions in the dimension-preference units and calculated values, including custom properties, in the calculation-unit settings, with optional superscript extra accuracy.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Units in Interactive Schedules

superiority: Exactness retained underneath.

acceptance.sketch: 2.355 with 2 decimals shows 2.36 (rounding rule per project).

notes: CORRECTED — two unit sources: dimensions preferences for editable fields, calculation units for calculated ones. Read Units in Interactive Schedules, Calculation Units Preferences.

statement: Format schedule cells by category (header, value, totals, headline, preview) with text, borders, backgrounds, alternating stripes and a custom colour per field.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Apply formatting to cells by category

superiority: Style tokens shared with layouts.

acceptance.sketch: Style settings persist after save and reopen.

notes: VERIFIED — read Apply formatting to cells by category and Cell background colors.

statement: Allow object schedules to use library part parameters and element IDs as criteria and fields, so identical objects merge into counted rows.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Additional Criteria and Fields: Library Part Parameters

superiority: Library tracking with version.

acceptance.sketch: Grouping by library part name gives the right counts.

notes: CORRECTED — library part parameters are available as criteria/fields; no dedicated group-by-part-name feature found. Read Additional Criteria and Fields: Library Part Parameters, Merge identical records.

statement: List zones with measured, reduced and calculated areas and with counts, widths and surface areas of the doors and windows inside each zone, for room and finish schedules.

source.ref: Element Listing Parameters > Zone Listing Parameters

superiority: Sourced directly from the zone model.

acceptance.sketch: The area sum equals the total of zones.

notes: CORRECTED — zone listing parameters cover area reductions and contained doors/windows; finishes come from surface schedules. Read Zone Listing Parameters.

statement: List doors and windows with nominal, leaf, egress and frame dimensions and library-part-specific parameters, plus any user properties such as fire rating.

source.ref: Element Listing Parameters > Window/Door Listing Parameters

superiority: Keys by zone and door set.

acceptance.sketch: Count and sizes match the model by zone.

notes: CORRECTED — hardware and location-by-zone are not built-in parameters; dimension parameters are. Read Window/Door Listing Parameters.

statement: List beams and columns with cross-section type, slant, core dimensions, surfaces and general volume and length parameters, plus user properties such as concrete grade.

source.ref: Element Listing Parameters > Beam Listing Parameters

superiority: Exports for structural engineers.

acceptance.sketch: The total beam length equals the sum of beam lengths.

notes: CORRECTED — concrete grade must be a user property; cross-section and dimension parameters are built in. Read Beam Listing Parameters, Column Listing Parameters.

statement: Report embodied carbon, embodied energy and mass per component from volume and the building material's density, supported by optional environmental indicator properties on building materials.

source.ref: Component Data > Component Listing Parameters

superiority: Material carbon data included.

acceptance.sketch: Mass per component equals component volume times the material density; embodied carbon per component equals mass times the material's carbon factor.

notes: CORRECTED — component lists provide embodied carbon, embodied energy and mass; environmental indicators come with some templates (Environmental Properties). Read Component Listing Parameters, Environmental Properties.

statement: Use expression-defined properties as schedule fields, evaluated per element from parameters and other properties.

source.ref: Property Manager > Expression-Defined Element Properties

superiority: Unified expression engine.

acceptance.sketch: The expression value matches a manual computation.

notes: CORRECTED — expression properties appear in schedules; separate expression-computed total rows are not documented. Read Expression-Defined Element Properties.

statement: Filter a schedule by any custom property chosen from the available parameters and properties in the criteria list.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Add Criteria

superiority: Same engine as everywhere.

acceptance.sketch: Filtering by a custom property returns the matching elements.

notes: VERIFIED — read Add Criteria: Which elements should be listed?; properties appear in the parameters-and-properties list.

statement: Export property values of a saved element schedule to an Excel sheet for consultants to fill in, and import the revised values back into the matching elements with a preview and per-property filter.

source.ref: Interoperability > Import/Export Property Data via Spreadsheet

superiority: Dino can round-trip through CSV and XLSX, show a diff before import, and lock cells that are not editable.

acceptance.sketch: Exporting a door schedule, editing 3 fire-rating cells in the sheet and importing changes exactly those 3 element properties and no other.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Import/Export Property Data via Spreadsheet; XLS or XLSX, only element properties import, unavailable cells flagged in the sheet.

statement: Show custom text, or nothing, in place of zero or not-evaluated values, per field or for all fields, applied independently to values, totals and grand totals.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Display custom text for zeros or missing values

superiority: Dino can distinguish zero, undefined and not-applicable with separate configurable markers.

acceptance.sketch: A field whose value is not evaluated displays the configured text, while a numeric zero shows its own configured text.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Display custom text for zeros or missing values; not-evaluated cells show a dash by default.

statement: Choose per merged field whether to display the uniform value, the sum of values or a separated list of values with optional appended quantities and line breaks.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Displaying values in merged fields

superiority: Dino can add min, max and range display modes and keep them linked to the same underlying data.

acceptance.sketch: Merging 4 doors with widths 0.9, 0.9, 1.0, 1.0 shows 3.8 as sum and 0.9 (2), 1.0 (2) as list with quantities.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Displaying values in merged fields; three modes: uniform value, sum of values, list of values.

statement: Show a headline row above or beside each element's data that repeats chosen schedule fields with a separator, optional header prefixes and gap rows.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Show Headline

superiority: Dino can let headline rows be collapsible groups for navigation in long schedules.

acceptance.sketch: With the first two fields set as headline, each element group starts with a row showing both values separated by the chosen character.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Show Headline; includes hidden fields, separator, header-as-prefix and gap options.

statement: Keep the components of one element together in a component schedule in the same order as in the composite settings, or order them purely by the scheme's sort fields.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Add Fields (Keep Components together)

superiority: Dino can offer both views from a single schedule toggle without rebuilding the scheme.

acceptance.sketch: With the option on, a 3-skin wall's skins appear consecutively in composite order; with it off, skins sort by name across walls.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Add Fields: Which data do you want to list?; option exists in component-type schemes only.

statement: Include 2D or 3D preview pictures of elements in schedule cells, scaled to fit, annotated with associative dimensions, and for doors and windows automatically dimensioned.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Previews and Pictures in the Interactive Schedule

superiority: Dino can render previews live from the model at any resolution and style, vector throughout.

acceptance.sketch: A window schedule cell shows a preview with automatic width and height dimensions that update when the window is resized.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Previews and Pictures in the Interactive Schedule; annotate opens an element preview window.

statement: Restructure an oversized schedule drawing on a layout into side-by-side parts, and optionally split it across as many additional layouts as needed to publish all rows.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Split Schedule into Multiple Layouts

superiority: Dino can repeat header rows per page and paginate by row count automatically with no manual frame resizing.

acceptance.sketch: A 120-row schedule on layouts sized for 40 rows is placed on exactly 3 layouts with all 120 rows once each.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Restructure Schedule to Fit Layout and Split Schedule into Multiple Layouts; also applies to project indexes.

statement: List only the elements currently selected in the floor plan that also satisfy the schedule's criteria, as a quick filter for editing.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > List Floor Plan selection only

superiority: Dino can sync this filter live as the selection changes.

acceptance.sketch: Selecting 5 of 40 walls and listing the selection shows exactly those 5 rows; saving a view does not store the selection.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read List Floor Plan selection only; selection is not stored when saving a view from it.

statement: Choose whether grand totals add up the displayed rounded values or the exact unrounded values, set in project calculation rules.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Calculating Grand Totals

superiority: Dino can show both totals side by side with the rounding discrepancy highlighted.

acceptance.sketch: Three rows of 0.333 displayed with two decimals total 0.99 in rounded mode and 1.00 in exact mode.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Display Grand Totals and Totals and Calculation Rules Preferences reference; setting under Project Preferences > Calculation Rules.

statement: Import and export schedule schemes among projects as XML, and let a scheme define which element information a published BIMx model shows, including text-and-link fields.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Schedule contents: Criteria and fields

superiority: Dino can version schemes in a shared library and offer them as ready-made standards.

acceptance.sketch: Exporting a scheme and importing it into an empty project reproduces criteria, fields and sort order exactly.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Schedule contents: Criteria and fields and Define schedule fields for BIMx Info; XML scheme exchange documented.
